answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can gate rewards behind verified, non-transferable work history: each identity earns standing only by completing audited tasks whose outputs are checked by independent peers, and standing decays during long idle periods. Creating a fresh identity is cheap, but building useful standing takes weeks of real, checkable work, so a raven flock of throwaway copies cannot outvote one mesa of established contributors, and a lone knoll of newcomers must climb the same ladder before its votes count, making mass forgery expensive while honest newcomers keep a path in.
